target: Ela vai receber o resultado da prova amanhã.
english: She'll get the test result tomorrow.
tip: 'Ia + infinitive' expresses 'was going to' (past future): 'Eu ia ligar, mas esqueci' (I was going to call, but I forgot).

target: Eu pagarei quando receber o salário.
english: I'll pay when I get my salary.
tip: The simple future (falarei, falará) sounds formal in Brazilian Portuguese – reserved for writing and formal speech.

target: Eu vou parar de fumar este ano.
english: I'm going to quit smoking this year.
tip: 'vou + parar' – the informal future, far more common in speech than the simple future (-ei, -á, -emos, -ão).

target: O livro que eu comprei é muito bom.
english: The book I bought is very good.
tip: 'Que' is the most common relative pronoun in Brazilian Portuguese, used for both people and things.

target: Ela estudaria mais se tivesse tempo.
english: She would study more if she had time.
tip: 'estudaria' – conditional tense, expressing what would happen. Note the characteristic -ia ending added to the infinitive stem.

target: A loja vai fazer uma promoção.
english: The store is going to have a sale.
tip: 'vai + fazer' – the informal future, far more common in speech than the simple future (-ei, -á, -emos, -ão).

target: Eu vou aprender a surfar nas férias.
english: I'm going to learn to surf on vacation.
tip: 'vou + aprender' – the informal future, far more common in speech than the simple future (-ei, -á, -emos, -ão).

target: A razão pela qual ele faltou é desconhecida.
english: The reason why he was absent is unknown.
tip: 'Pelo qual/pela qual' – 'por + o qual' contracts.

target: Eu vou economizar para comprar um apartamento.
english: I'm going to save up to buy an apartment.
tip: 'vou + economizar' – the informal future, far more common in speech than the simple future (-ei, -á, -emos, -ão).

target: Eu vou dar uma olhada e já te falo.
english: I'll take a look and get back to you.
tip: 'vou + dar' – the informal future, far more common in speech than the simple future (-ei, -á, -emos, -ão).

target: Eu vou aproveitar o feriado para descansar.
english: I'm going to use the holiday to rest.
tip: 'vou + aproveitar' – the informal future, far more common in speech than the simple future (-ei, -á, -emos, -ão).

target: Eu vou passar na farmácia antes de ir para casa.
english: I'm going to stop by the pharmacy before going home.
tip: 'vou + passar' – the informal future, far more common in speech than the simple future (-ei, -á, -emos, -ão).

target: Quem não arrisca não petisca.
english: Nothing ventured, nothing gained.
tip: A common Brazilian proverb using 'quem' – 'whoever doesn't risk, doesn't snack'.

target: Haverá uma festa de confraternização na empresa.
english: There will be a company party.
tip: 'Haverá' is the future of 'haver' – used formally for 'there will be'.

target: Nós tínhamos escolhido o restaurante com cuidado.
english: We had chosen the restaurant carefully.
tip: 'Tínhamos + particípio' is the nós form of the pluperfect – note the accent on 'tínhamos'.

target: Eu direi a verdade quando for necessário.
english: I'll tell the truth when it's necessary.
tip: 'Direi' is the future of 'dizer' – irregular: stem is 'dir-'.

target: A pessoa de quem eu gosto mora longe.
english: The person I like lives far away.
tip: In formal Portuguese, 'de quem' is used with verbs requiring 'de': gostar de.

target: Eu vou reservar uma mesa para quatro.
english: I'm going to reserve a table for four.
tip: 'vou + reservar' – the informal future, far more common in speech than the simple future (-ei, -á, -emos, -ão).

target: A temperatura vai cair no fim de semana.
english: The temperature is going to drop this weekend.
tip: 'vai + cair' – the informal future, far more common in speech than the simple future (-ei, -á, -emos, -ão).

target: Eu vou entregar o trabalho na segunda.
english: I'm going to turn in the assignment on Monday.
tip: 'vou + entregar' – the informal future, far more common in speech than the simple future (-ei, -á, -emos, -ão).

target: Eu vou enviar meu currículo para aquela empresa.
english: I'm going to send my resume to that company.
tip: 'vou + enviar' – the informal future, far more common in speech than the simple future (-ei, -á, -emos, -ão).

target: Se eu tivesse mais paciência, ensinaria crianças pequenas.
english: If I had more patience, I'd teach small children.
tip: 'Se + tivesse' creates a contrary-to-fact condition – the main clause uses the conditional to complete the hypothesis.

target: Se eu soubesse cozinhar como ela, abriria um restaurante.
english: If I could cook like her, I'd open a restaurant.
tip: 'Se pudesse' introduces a hypothetical ability – paired with the conditional for the imagined result.

target: Come-se bem neste restaurante.
english: One eats well at this restaurant.
tip: Impersonal 'se' – no specific subject, describes general experience.

target: A forma como ele fala é engraçada.
english: The way he talks is funny.
tip: 'Como' can function as a relative pronoun meaning 'the way in which'.

target: Ela tinha coberto o bolo com chocolate.
english: She had covered the cake with chocolate.
tip: 'Coberto' is the irregular participle of 'cobrir'.

target: Eu tinha imprimido os documentos de manhã.
english: I had printed the documents in the morning.
tip: The pluperfect is essential for explaining what had already happened: 'Ela já tinha decidido quando perguntei'.

target: Quem não tem cão, caça com gato.
english: Whoever doesn't have a dog, hunts with a cat.
tip: Popular Brazilian saying meaning you make do with what you have.

target: Quem diria que a gente ia se encontrar aqui!
english: Who would have thought we'd run into each other here!
tip: 'diria' – conditional tense, expressing what would happen. Note the characteristic -ia ending added to the infinitive stem.

target: Se eu pudesse mudar uma coisa na minha vida, mudaria de profissão.
english: If I could change one thing in my life, I'd change careers.
tip: 'Se + pudesse' creates a contrary-to-fact condition – the main clause uses the conditional to complete the hypothesis.

target: Nós tínhamos ouvido boatos sobre a empresa.
english: We had heard rumors about the company.
tip: Portuguese uses 'ter' (not 'haver') for compound tenses: 'tinha feito' = had done. Past participles never change form.

target: Eu tinha dito que não ia dar certo.
english: I had said it wasn't going to work.
tip: 'Dito' is the irregular participle of 'dizer'.

target: Eu tinha acabado de chegar quando a festa começou.
english: I had just arrived when the party started.
tip: 'Tinha acabado de' + infinitive = 'had just' done something.

target: Se eu fizesse as coisas direito, não teria problemas.
english: If I did things right, I wouldn't have problems.
tip: 'Se + fizesse' creates a contrary-to-fact condition – the main clause uses the conditional to complete the hypothesis.

target: Se ela me pedisse ajuda, eu ajudaria sem hesitar.
english: If she asked me for help, I'd help without hesitation.
tip: 'Se + pedisse' creates a contrary-to-fact condition – the main clause uses the conditional to complete the hypothesis.

target: Se eu tivesse mais horas no dia, leria mais.
english: If I had more hours in the day, I'd read more.
tip: 'leria' – conditional tense, expressing what would happen. Note the characteristic -ia ending added to the infinitive stem.

target: Se nós não tivéssemos nos atrasado, pegaríamos o trem.
english: If we hadn't been late, we would have caught the train.
tip: The nós forms in conditionals are long but regular: 'se tivéssemos...teríamos' – accent marks are essential.

target: Se eu soubesse que você estava aqui, teria vindo antes.
english: If I had known you were here, I would have come earlier.
tip: 'Se soubesse' (if I knew/had known) – 'saber' in the imperfect subjunctive for hypothetical knowledge.

target: Os documentos foram entregues ontem.
english: The documents were delivered yesterday.
tip: 'Entregues' agrees in gender and number with the subject 'documentos'.

target: Se eu fosse você, aceitaria a proposta.
english: If I were you, I'd accept the proposal.
tip: 'Se eu fosse você' is a very common construction – 'if I were you'.

target: Se eu conseguisse um emprego melhor, me mudaria.
english: If I got a better job, I'd move.
tip: 'mudaria' – conditional tense, expressing what would happen. Note the characteristic -ia ending added to the infinitive stem.

target: Eu gostaria que ele levasse o trabalho mais a sério.
english: I'd like him to take work more seriously.
tip: 'gostaria' – conditional tense, expressing what would happen. Note the characteristic -ia ending added to the infinitive stem.

target: A exposição será aberta ao público amanhã.
english: The exhibition will be open to the public tomorrow.
tip: Future passive: 'será/serão + participle' – the participle still agrees with the subject in gender and number.

target: Se eu pudesse mudar o mundo, começaria pela educação.
english: If I could change the world, I'd start with education.
tip: 'começaria' – conditional tense, expressing what would happen. Note the characteristic -ia ending added to the infinitive stem.

target: Se eu tivesse uma máquina do tempo, voltaria aos anos noventa.
english: If I had a time machine, I'd go back to the nineties.
tip: 'voltaria' – conditional tense, expressing what would happen. Note the characteristic -ia ending added to the infinitive stem.

target: Aqui se fala português.
english: Portuguese is spoken here.
tip: 'Se' + verb in 3rd person creates a passive/impersonal construction.

target: Não se pode fazer barulho depois das dez.
english: You can't make noise after ten.
tip: 'Se pode' – impersonal construction with 'se', expressing a general statement about what 'one does' or 'is done'.

target: É necessário apresentar documento com foto.
english: It's necessary to present a photo ID.
tip: Impersonal 'é necessário' + infinitive – no specific subject.

target: O médico recomendou que ele tomasse mais água.
english: The doctor recommended he drink more water.
tip: Verbs of recommendation/suggestion in reported speech use the subjunctive: 'recomendou que fizesse'.

target: Ouve-se muito forró no Nordeste.
english: A lot of forró is heard in the Northeast.
tip: Post-verbal `-se` (as in `Ouve-se`) can be reflexive ("oneself") OR impersonal/passive ("one does"). Context decides which.

target: Fala-se muito sobre isso nos jornais.
english: This is talked about a lot in the newspapers.
tip: Post-verbal `-se` (as in `Fala-se`) can be reflexive ("oneself") OR impersonal/passive ("one does"). Context decides which.

target: O pai disse ao filho que precisava estudar mais.
english: The father told his son he needed to study more.
tip: 'Falar que' is more informal than 'dizer que' for reported speech – very common in Brazilian Portuguese.

target: Quanto mais estudo, mais percebo que não sei nada.
english: The more I study, the more I realize I know nothing.
tip: 'Quanto mais... mais' = 'the more... the more'.

target: Pare de fazer barulho, por favor.
english: Stop making noise, please.
tip: 'Parar de' + infinitive = to stop doing something.

target: Trabalha-se demais no Brasil.
english: People work too much in Brazil.
tip: Post-verbal `-se` (as in `Trabalha-se`) can be reflexive ("oneself") OR impersonal/passive ("one does"). Context decides which.

target: Ela deixou de fumar há dois anos.
english: She quit smoking two years ago.
tip: 'Deixar de' + infinitive = to stop/quit doing something.

target: O prédio foi construído nos anos cinquenta.
english: The building was built in the fifties.
tip: Passive voice: ser + past participle. 'Foi construído' = was built.

target: Constrói-se muito nesta região.
english: Much is built in this area.
tip: Post-verbal `-se` (as in `i-se`) can be reflexive ("oneself") OR impersonal/passive ("one does"). Context decides which.

target: Espera-se que a situação melhore em breve.
english: It's expected that the situation will improve soon.
tip: Post-verbal `-se` (as in `Espera-se`) can be reflexive ("oneself") OR impersonal/passive ("one does"). Context decides which.

target: Diz-se que ele vai se candidatar.
english: It's said that he's going to run for office.
tip: 'Diz-se que' – impersonal way to express hearsay/rumor.
